issues.legal_issue: An interlocutory mandatory injunction transferring possession should not be granted when possession is admitted, entitlement to possession remains for trial, and no exceptional basis for disturbing the status quo is established.
material_facts: The plaintiff brought a suit for possession, alleging that the defendant’s licence had expired, and sought an interlocutory order transferring possession before trial.
The defendant’s possession, directly or through a caretaker, was admitted, while the nature of the parties’ relationship and the plaintiff’s entitlement to possession remained unresolved.
The trial court declined to order interim possession because doing so would effectively decree the suit before trial.
The appellate court ordered the defendant to transfer possession, relying in part on the property’s disuse and the circumstances of the litigation.
The Supreme Court found that the case fell within none of the exceptional circumstances permitting an interlocutory mandatory injunction.
issues.conclusion: The appellate court’s mandatory interim order was set aside and the trial court’s refusal to grant interim possession was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under Dorab Cawasji Warden v. Coomi Sorab Warden, 1990 (2) SCC 117, interlocutory mandatory injunctions are granted only in exceptional cases, generally to preserve or restore the last uncontested status quo or to undo an illegal act or restore something wrongfully taken. Granting possession before trial is not justified where the plaintiff’s entitlement remains undecided and no such exception applies. The property’s disuse, the defendant’s lack of beneficial use, potential damages, and the characterization of litigation as a luxury are irrelevant to changing the status quo of possession.

rule.if: interim_mandatory_injunction_in_possession_suit and defendant_possession_admitted and plaintiff_entitlement_unresolved and not exceptional_basis_for_disturbing_status_quo

predicates.interim_mandatory_injunction_in_possessi: A plaintiff in a suit seeking possession asks the court to order the defendant to transfer possession before trial.
predicates.defendant_possession_admitted: The parties admit that the defendant holds possession, directly or through an agent.
predicates.plaintiff_entitlement_unresolved: The court has not yet determined at trial whether the plaintiff is entitled to possession.
predicates.exceptional_basis_for_disturbing_status_: The facts establish an exceptional basis for a mandatory interim order, such as restoring the last uncontested status quo or undoing an illegal act or wrongful taking.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff seeks mandatory interim possession in a possession suit, the defendant’s possession is admitted, entitlement remains unresolved, and no exceptional basis for disturbing the status quo exists, the interim possession order is denied.

issues.legal_issue: A receiver should not be appointed to manage possession during a pending possession suit when that appointment is unnecessary to maintain the existing possession arrangement.
material_facts: A receiver had been appointed in the pending possession suit.
The appellate court directed the receiver to inventory the property’s movable items, take symbolic possession, and place the plaintiff in possession under the receiver’s authority.
The Supreme Court held that the receiver’s appointment to supervise possession was unnecessary and set it aside along with the appellate order.
issues.conclusion: The appointment of the receiver to supervise possession was set aside as unnecessary.
issues.legal_principle: Where an interim order transferring possession is unwarranted, the appointment of a receiver to supervise possession of the property is also unnecessary on the circumstances stated in the judgment.

predicates.receiver_appointed_for_possession_manage: The court appoints a receiver to manage or supervise possession of property while a suit is pending.
predicates.possession_suit_pending: A suit seeking a determination of entitlement to possession remains pending.
predicates.interim_transfer_of_possession_unwarrant: The circumstances do not justify transferring possession before the suit is decided.

issues.definition: When a receiver is appointed to manage possession during a pending possession suit and an interim transfer of possession is unwarranted, the receiver’s appointment for possession management is set aside.
